q: Which suppliers should I ask for emissions data first?
title: Which suppliers to ask for data first
short: Start with the few suppliers behind most of your estimated Scope 3 emissions, not most of your spend. Rank purchases by spend or quantity times a rough factor, take the suppliers that make up about 80% of the total, then move up anyone selling CBAM goods or whom your buyer names.

ol: Export a year of purchases by supplier, with spend, quantity, unit and HSN code.
Assign each supplier a rough factor for what they sell: a spend-based factor per rupee, or a material factor per tonne where you know the quantity.
Multiply and rank. The point is the order, not the exact tonnes; screening factors can be off by a wide margin and are fine for this job.

sections.h: Step 2: apply the GHG Protocol screening criteria
p: The Scope 3 Standard (chapter 6) suggests weighing more than size. After ranking by estimated emissions, move a supplier up the list if:
ul: You have influence: a large share of their sales, a long contract, or a renewal coming up.
They create risk: CBAM-covered goods such as steel, aluminium or fertilisers, where actual data cuts your EU buyer's cost.
A stakeholder asks: your customer, lender or an SBTi target names that category.
You outsourced a process you used to run, such as heat treatment or plating, because those emissions used to sit in your own Scope 1 and 2.
Large spend with low emissions: software, professional services, rent. Spend-based estimates are good enough.
Traders who resell without processing, unless you can reach the manufacturer behind them.
One-off purchases you will not repeat next year.

sections.h: A decision rule for the first round
p: Ask the top five to ten suppliers by estimated emissions, plus any CBAM-goods supplier, for activity data or a product footprint. Use averages for everyone else this year, and redo the ranking each year as supplier data replaces estimates.

For those priority purchases, the GHG Protocol guidance names the kinds of supplier to approach: contract manufacturers, materials and parts suppliers, capital equipment suppliers, fuel suppliers, third-party logistics providers, waste management companies and other providers of goods and services.

example.title: Worked example: ranking six supplier groups
lines: Steel coil: ₹200 lakh x 4.0 t CO2e per lakh = 800 t
Machining job work: ₹80 lakh x 0.5 = 40 t
Total: ₹600 lakh and 1,263 t; steel and aluminium are 1,050 t, about 83% of emissions on 42% of spend
example.note: Factors here are example figures chosen to show the method, not published values. Among single suppliers, job work is second by spend but fourth by emissions.

senseible: Senseible reads purchase invoices and keeps spend, quantity and HSN code by supplier in a separate supplier evidence trail, which gives you the list to rank. The reader does not apply spend-based factors on its own; for the screen, use the supplier emissions risk calculator, your own factors, or a spend-based estimate from Senseible, labelled as such.
